1) Freshly ground meat. As fresh as you can manage. If that means asking the butcher to grind a steak, so be it.

2) Fat is flavor. Leaner meat isn't your friend, here.

3) Season the meat before cooking. A little salt, a little pepper, MSG, maybe some onion and garlic powders. Mix thoroughly before forming patties.

4) Not too thick. The longer it takes the heat to get through to the middle, the morest chance you have to burn the outside.
Take your thumb and dimple the top of the patty, right in the middle. Not too deep, about halfway through. Stops your patties from turning into burger balls.
